Las 4 fases de un ataque social: The 4 phases of a social attack
Un ataque de ingeniería social rara vez: A social engineering attack is rarely improvised: it usually follows a cycle with four recognizable phases. First, research, where the attacker gathers public information about the victim or organization, often from social networks or corporate websites. Then comes building rapport, where they make contact and create a relationship of apparent trust or authority. Next, exploitation, the moment they ask for the concrete action: clicking a link, transferring money or revealing a password, relying on urgency or fear. Finally, the exit, where the attacker withdraws, trying to leave no trace or raise immediate suspicion. Recognizing which phase a suspicious interaction is in helps cut the attack short before it reaches the point of exploitation.
Explica los principios psicológicos que: Explains the psychological principles attackers use to manipulate their victims.
Describe las fases típicas de un ataque,: Describes the typical phases of an attack, from research to exploitation.
Explica por qué las personas suelen ser: Explains why people are usually the most vulnerable link in security.
Por qué atacan a las personas, no sistem: Why they attack people, not systems
Los sistemas técnicos pueden parchearse,: Technical systems can be patched, but human behavior responds to psychological patterns that are much harder to "update": we trust authority figures, we want to help when someone seems to need it, and we act faster and with less judgment under time pressure. That's why it's usually easier and cheaper for an attacker to convince a person to hand over a password than to breach a well-configured firewall. This is the reason social engineering remains, year after year, one of the most effective attack vectors in real security incidents, no matter how much an organization invests in technology. No tool replaces the judgment of a person trained to detect when something doesn't add up, however urgent or convincing it seems.
Los atacantes se apoyan en principios de: Attackers rely on principles of persuasion well documented by social psychology. Authority, posing as a boss, vendor or official body to reduce questioning. Urgency, forcing quick decisions before the victim can calmly verify the request. Reciprocity, offering something first (a favor, a gift) to create a sense of debt. Social proof, suggesting that "others already did it" to normalize the requested action. And scarcity, hinting that an opportunity will disappear if they don't act immediately. None of these principles is bad in itself, since they're also used in legitimate marketing, but combined with a false identity they become tools of manipulation. Recognizing them in the moment is the first step to resisting them.
Phishing, smishing, vishing y ataques di: Phishing, smishing, vishing and targeted attacks
Enseña a reconocer las características t: Teaches how to recognize the typical characteristics of a phishing email.

El phishing por correo electrónico sigue: Email phishing is still the most common social engineering vector: messages that impersonate a bank, vendor or coworker, asking you to click a link, download an attachment or confirm details "urgently". They often imitate the design of well-known brands quite faithfully, but give themselves away through signs such as slightly altered sender domains, writing errors, generic greetings instead of personalized ones, and links whose real destination (visible when hovering over them) doesn't match the text shown. Faced with any email asking for an action with unusual urgency, the safest thing is not to click the links in the message and instead go directly to the official website by typing the address in the browser, or contact the organization through an already known channel.
Phishing por SMS y llamadas: Phishing by SMS and phone calls
El smishing es phishing por mensaje de t: Smishing is phishing by text message, and vishing is its phone call version; both take advantage of the fact that people tend to lower their guard outside of email, where there's already more of a habit of being suspicious. An SMS announcing a held package with a "customs payment" link, or a call from a supposed bank agent warning about a suspicious charge and asking you to confirm a code, are typical examples of each technique. These channels create a sense of immediacy and personalization that's hard to replicate by email, which makes them especially effective. No legitimate entity, whether a bank, customs or technical support, will ask for passwords, verification codes or your full card number by phone or text message; when in doubt, the right thing is to hang up and call back an official number you've verified yourself.
A diferencia del phishing masivo, el spe: Unlike mass phishing, spear phishing targets a specific person or position, using real information gathered beforehand (the boss's name, ongoing projects, usual vendors) to be much more convincing. Business Email Compromise (BEC) takes this a step further in the corporate environment: the attacker impersonates a real executive or vendor, often by compromising or spoofing their email account, to request an urgent bank transfer or a change of payment details, causing multimillion-dollar losses to companies around the world. The most effective defense isn't only technical but procedural: any bank account change or unusual transfer must be verified through a second channel, such as a phone call to that person's already known number, before carrying it out.
El cebo del USB abandonado: The bait of the abandoned USB drive
El baiting explota la curiosidad humana: Baiting exploits human curiosity by offering a physical or digital "bait": the classic example is leaving a USB drive abandoned in an office parking lot or reception area, with an eye-catching label such as "confidential" or "payroll", in the hope that someone will plug it into their computer out of curiosity. That device can contain malware that installs automatically when connected, without needing to open any file. There are digital variants, such as offers of free software downloads or pirated content that actually install malicious software. The practical rule is simple: any USB device of unknown origin must not be connected to a personal or corporate computer under any circumstances, and should be handed over to the security or IT area if found on an organization's premises.
Técnicas de manipulación presenciales y: In-person and social media manipulation techniques

Las redes sociales son una mina de infor: Social networks are a gold mine of information for attackers: posts about a new job, a pet, a vacation or a family member's name are often precisely the answers to security questions or the details that make a later pretext believable. An attacker can use this information to create fake profiles that look like real acquaintances, send friend requests to access private content, or craft a highly personalized, convincing phishing message. Reviewing and limiting each network's privacy settings, thinking twice before posting details that reveal routines or sensitive data, and being wary of contact requests from profiles with little activity or few mutual connections considerably reduces the attack surface available for this type of manipulation.
El pretexting consiste en construir una: Pretexting consists of building a believable false story or identity to justify a request that would otherwise raise suspicion: an attacker can pose as technical support who needs to "verify" a password, an external auditor who requires temporary access to a system, or a new coworker from another office asking for help with an urgent task. Unlike mass phishing, it usually requires more preparation on the attacker's part, including real details about the organization or the person being impersonated to sound legitimate. The main defense is to institutionalize verification: no request for access, a password change or sensitive information should be granted just because the person asking "sounds" convincing, but because their identity was confirmed through an independent, already established channel.
Ciertas características se repiten en la: Certain characteristics repeat in the vast majority of social engineering attempts, regardless of the channel used: artificial urgency ("you must act now or you'll lose access"), requests for information the organization would never ask for through that medium (passwords, verification codes), pressure to skip a normal verification process, and subtle errors in domains, phone numbers or names that almost match the legitimate ones but not exactly. Another key sign is the mismatch between the channel used and the seriousness of the request: a bank account change requested over chat, or a dismissal communicated by SMS, doesn't fit the usual formal processes. Training yourself to notice this mismatch, rather than memorizing specific examples, is what really protects you against new techniques that aren't known yet.
Señales de alerta y verificación de soli: Warning signs and verification of suspicious requests
Enseña señales de alerta comunes ante so: Teaches common warning signs in unusual requests for information or money.

Muchas organizaciones envían campañas de: Many organizations send simulated phishing campaigns to their own employees, not to punish whoever clicks, but to realistically measure how prepared the human team is against a real attempt. The training value lies in the moment after the click: whoever falls for the simulation immediately receives an explanation of which signs they should have noticed, turning the mistake into concrete learning instead of a sanction. Seeing these simulations as an opportunity to practice, and not as a trap to point fingers, significantly improves their effectiveness. Organizations with the best results usually repeat these exercises periodically, varying the simulated techniques, since detection ability degrades over time if it isn't constantly reinforced.
La forma más confiable de neutralizar un: The most reliable way to neutralize a social engineering attempt is simple: if someone requests something unusual or sensitive through one channel (email, chat, a call), verify their identity using a different, previously known channel, never the number or link the suspicious request itself provides. If an email claims to be from the bank, call the official number printed on the card, not the one in the message. If a "boss" asks for an urgent transfer over chat, call the cell phone number you already had saved. This principle, known as out-of-band verification, is so effective because an attacker rarely controls both channels at the same time, so a second independent contact usually exposes the impersonation immediately.
Cada intento de ingeniería social, exito: Every social engineering attempt, successful or not, is a valuable source of information about what tactics attackers are currently using against a specific person or organization. Analyzing what made the scam believable, which channel was used and which warning sign went unnoticed makes it possible to adjust both personal judgment and organizational controls for the future. This learning should be shared, within the team or the family, without shame about having fallen or nearly fallen for the scam, since silence only benefits the attacker and leaves others exposed to the same technique. Organizations with the best security culture treat every reported incident as an opportunity for collective improvement, not as a reason for individual sanctions.

Primeros pasos si caíste en un engaño: First steps if you fell for a scam
Si ya se hizo clic en un enlace malicios: If you've already clicked a malicious link, handed over a password or made a transfer under false pretenses, acting fast reduces the damage far more than regretting it. The first steps include immediately changing the passwords involved (from a different device if possible), enabling multi-factor authentication if it wasn't active, contacting the bank to block or reverse a suspicious transaction, and disconnecting the device from the network if malware is suspected. Just as important is immediately informing the security or IT area if it happened in a work context, instead of trying to fix it quietly out of fear of the consequences: the sooner the incident is known, the faster its impact on other connected systems or people can be contained.
El tiempo entre caer en un engaño y repo: The time between falling for a scam and reporting it is often the factor that most determines the final damage: a card blocked five minutes later prevents charges that one blocked the next day can no longer stop. Reporting immediately, whether to the bank, the company's security area or the affected platform, makes it possible to start containment before the attacker uses the information obtained on other related systems or accounts. Many organizations have a specific, fast channel for this type of report, and knowing it in advance, before you need it, saves critical minutes. Reporting shouldn't be postponed while waiting for absolute certainty: if there's reasonable doubt that you've been the victim of a scam, it's better to over-report than to stay quiet for fear of being wrong.

DevSecOps parte de una idea simple: la s: DevSecOps starts from a simple idea: security can't be a final review before going to production, because by then fixing a problem is much more expensive and slower than if it had been detected during development. In practice, this means integrating automated security controls into the same pipeline development and operations teams already use, instead of creating a separate process run exclusively by a security team. Code analysis tools, dependency scanning and automated tests run on every change, giving the developer feedback in minutes instead of weeks. The cultural change is as important as the technical one: every developer becomes responsible for the security of their own code, not just for it working correctly.
Principios de seguridad en el ciclo de v: Security principles in the software lifecycle
Introduce los principios de seguridad ap: Introduces the security principles applicable to each stage of software development.
Explica cómo integrar prácticas de segur: Explains how to continuously integrate security practices into DevOps workflows.
Presenta la metodología de modelado de a: Presents the threat modeling methodology for anticipating design risks.
El threat modeling consiste en identific: Threat modeling consists of systematically identifying what can go wrong in an application before writing the first line of code, instead of discovering it later through a real incident. A widely used approach is STRIDE, which evaluates each system component against six threat categories: spoofing, tampering, repudiation, information disclosure, denial of service and elevation of privilege. The result isn't a document that gets filed away, but a concrete list of mitigations built directly into the design: which data to encrypt, which validations to add, which permissions to restrict. Doing it early in the design, and not as a later audit, makes it possible to correct architectural decisions that would be much costlier to change once the system is already in production.
Seguridad en cada etapa del SDLC: Security at every stage of the SDLC
El desarrollo seguro no es una fase, sin: Secure development isn't a phase, but a set of practices that runs through the entire software development lifecycle (SDLC), from requirements to maintenance in production. In requirements and design, controls are defined and threats are modeled; in coding, secure standards and code review are applied; in testing, static and dynamic analysis is run in addition to functional tests; in deployment, the environment's secure configuration is verified; and in maintenance, patches are managed and behavior in production is monitored. The central principle is "shift left": moving security controls as early as possible in the cycle, because a defect detected in design costs a fraction of what it costs to fix the same flaw once the software is already in the hands of real users.
Cómo gestionar secretos sin exponerlos: How to manage secrets without exposing them
Claves de API, contraseñas de bases de d: API keys, database passwords and access tokens are high-value targets, and one of the most common mistakes (and most sought after by attackers) is leaving them written directly in source code or in configuration files pushed to a repository. The right practice is to use a dedicated secrets manager, such as Vault, AWS Secrets Manager or similar, which delivers credentials to the application at runtime without them being exposed in the code or the version control history. In addition, each secret should have the minimum necessary scope and be rotated periodically, so that if one leaks, the damage is limited in time and in the scope of compromised systems. Automated scanning tools can detect secrets accidentally committed before they reach production.
Repasa las vulnerabilidades más comunes: Reviews the most common application vulnerabilities and how to prevent them.
Enseña buenas prácticas para almacenar y: Teaches best practices for storing and handling credentials and keys securely.
Explica cómo prevenir vulnerabilidades m: Explains how to prevent vulnerabilities through data validation and secure error handling.
Vulnerabilidades más comunes según OWASP: The most common vulnerabilities according to OWASP
El OWASP Top 10 es la referencia más usa: The OWASP Top 10 is the most widely used reference for prioritizing web application security risks, and although it changes from edition to edition, certain categories stay constant: broken access control (letting a user access data that doesn't belong to them), injection (SQL, commands or other unvalidated data that ends up being executed), poor security configuration, and use of components with known vulnerabilities that haven't been updated. It's not a list to memorize but a guide for prioritizing effort: a team with limited resources gets more security value from systematically reviewing these categories than from trying to cover every possible vulnerability in a scattered way. Many of these flaws are prevented with simple practices, such as never trusting unvalidated input data and applying the principle of least privilege in every component.
Validar entradas y manejar errores bien: Validating inputs and handling errors well
Casi toda vulnerabilidad de inyección, y: Almost every injection vulnerability, whether SQL, command or browser script injection, originates from trusting input data without properly validating it before processing it. The basic rule is simple but often forgotten: all input coming from a user, an external API or a file must be treated as potentially malicious until its expected format, length and content are validated. Error handling is just as important: an overly detailed error message that reveals a database's structure or a framework's exact version gives an attacker valuable information. Errors should be logged in detail in internal logs for the development team, but shown to the user generically, without exposing technical details of the system that generated them.
A diferencia del análisis estático, que: Unlike static analysis, which reviews source code without running it, dynamic analysis (DAST) tests the application while it's running, sending it real malicious inputs to observe how it responds, much as an external attacker would. This makes it possible to detect problems that only appear at runtime, such as insecure server configurations or authentication flaws. Pentesting takes this a step further: a human specialist actively tries to break into the application, combining automated tools with creativity and knowledge of real attack techniques, something no automated tool fully replicates. Both approaches are complementary: DAST runs continuously and cheaply, while pentesting is reserved for deeper periodic assessments, typically before major launches.
Las herramientas de análisis estático (S: Static analysis tools (SAST) review source code without needing to run it, looking for known vulnerability patterns: insecure use of cryptographic functions, possible SQL injections, credentials written directly into the code or incorrect handling of sensitive data. Their big advantage is that they integrate directly into the developer's workflow, flagging the problem in the editor itself or in the pull request, before the code even reaches a test environment. They don't replace human review or other security testing, since they generate false positives and don't detect business logic flaws, but they work as a first automated line of defense, cheap and fast, that catches common mistakes before they become exploitable vulnerabilities in production.
Gestionar riesgo de librerías externas: Managing the risk of external libraries
El código propio de una aplicación suele: An application's own code is usually a small fraction of everything that actually runs: most of it is third-party libraries and frameworks, each with its own potential vulnerabilities that are constantly being discovered and published. Software composition analysis (SCA) automatically scans these dependencies, comparing them against public databases of known vulnerabilities, and alerts when a library used in the project has a reported flaw, also indicating whether a fixed version is available. Ignoring this layer of risk is common and dangerous: large-scale incidents, such as the Log4j vulnerability, spread precisely because many organizations didn't know for sure which projects used that library. Keeping an up-to-date inventory of dependencies is as important as writing your own secure code.
Presenta el uso de herramientas de análi: Presents the use of static analysis tools to detect vulnerabilities in code.
Explica cómo se prueban aplicaciones en: Explains how running applications are tested to identify real vulnerabilities.

Mezclar los ambientes de desarrollo, pru: Mixing development, test and production environments is one of the most common ways real customer data ends up exposed in environments with much less protection, or an experimental change directly affects real users. Segregating these environments means not just separate infrastructure, but also differentiated access control: not every developer needs access to production, and those who have it should go through an approval process with that action being logged. Data used in testing should ideally be anonymized or synthetic, avoiding copying production databases directly into environments with looser controls. This clear separation reduces both the risk of data leaks and the impact of a human error during development or testing.
Los contenedores y la infraestructura co: Containers and infrastructure as code (IaC) greatly speed up application deployment, but they can also replicate insecure configurations at scale if not managed carefully: an outdated or misconfigured base image automatically becomes hundreds of vulnerable instances. Best practices include scanning container images for vulnerabilities before publishing them to a registry, avoiding running processes inside the container with administrator privileges, and treating infrastructure definition files (such as Terraform or Kubernetes templates) with the same review rigor as the application code. An error in an IaC configuration file can accidentally expose a storage bucket or an entire database to the internet, so reviewing it shouldn't be treated as a minor detail.
Seguridad en CI/CD, contenedores e infra: Security in CI/CD, containers and infrastructure
Explica cómo incorporar controles de seg: Explains how to build security controls into continuous integration and deployment processes.
Presenta buenas prácticas de seguridad p: Presents security best practices for containers and automated deployments.
Enseña la importancia de separar y prote: Teaches the importance of separating and protecting development, test and production environments.
El pipeline de integración y despliegue: The continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD) pipeline is itself an attractive target for an attacker: whoever manages to compromise it can inject malicious code directly into the build process, affecting every version published afterward. Protecting the pipeline means restricting who can modify its configuration, signing and verifying the artifacts generated at each stage, and using minimum-scope, temporary credentials for each deployment step, instead of a single key with full, permanent access. Integrating automated security controls into the pipeline itself (code, dependency and image scanning) ensures no change reaches production without passing those validations, without depending on a human remembering to run them manually every time.
Una vulnerabilidad conocida y sin correg: A known, unpatched vulnerability is easier for an attacker to exploit than an unknown one, because there's already public documentation and sometimes even proof-of-concept code available. That's why having a formal patch management process, which identifies available updates, assesses their criticality and applies them within a defined time frame according to severity, is as important as any other security control. Many organizations fail not because they don't know a patch exists, but because they don't have a clear process for testing and deploying it quickly without breaking the application in production. Automating this process where possible, and prioritizing updates to components with actively exploited critical vulnerabilities, significantly reduces the window of exposure to known attacks.
Mantenimiento seguro de aplicaciones en: Secure maintenance of applications in production
Explica la importancia de mantener actua: Explains the importance of keeping software components up to date.
Presenta cómo estos programas ayudan a i: Presents how these programs help identify vulnerabilities collaboratively.
Enseña la importancia del monitoreo cons: Teaches the importance of constant monitoring to detect anomalous behavior.
Vigilar la app ya en producción: Watching the app once it's in production
Ninguna aplicación es completamente segu: No application is completely secure once deployed, so continuous monitoring in production acts as the last layer of defense when something slipped past earlier testing. This includes logging and analyzing access and error logs for anomalous patterns, such as repeated failed authentication attempts or requests trying to exploit undocumented routes, and having automatic alerts that notify the team when out-of-the-ordinary behavior occurs. Application performance monitoring (APM) tools and intrusion detection systems help identify within minutes what, without proper visibility, could go unnoticed for weeks. An incident detected and contained in time, thanks to good monitoring, costs a fraction of one discovered by a customer or the press.
Un programa de bug bounty invita a inves: A bug bounty program invites external security researchers to look for vulnerabilities in an application in exchange for a financial reward, leveraging the creativity of a community much broader than any internal team. To work well, it needs clear rules: which systems are in scope, what types of testing are allowed, and a direct communication channel with the security team. Responsible disclosure is the principle that sustains it: the researcher reports the flaw privately and gives the organization time to fix it before making it public, preventing it from being exposed to other attackers in the meantime. Well managed, this type of program complements internal testing with a constant, external source of detection of real vulnerabilities.

Simplemente... Proteger la niñez y la ju: Simply... protecting children and young people, our everything as a society.
Cada foto, comentario o partida de un vi: Every photo, comment or video game match shared online is part of a child's or teenager's digital footprint, a trail that can follow them for years and is often built without them, or their parents, being fully aware of it. That information can be used by third parties to profile them, contact them or even impersonate them later on. As a responsible adult, it's not about banning all digital presence, but about accompanying concrete decisions: reviewing each app's privacy settings together, avoiding posting details such as their school or real-time location, and explaining that what goes on the internet rarely disappears completely, even if it's later deleted.
El entorno digital que habitan niños y a: The digital environment children and teenagers live in
Presenta un panorama de las plataformas: Presents an overview of the most popular digital platforms among children and teenagers.
Explica cómo varían los riesgos digitale: Explains how digital risks vary according to the child's age and maturity.
Aborda la importancia de cuidar la infor: Covers the importance of taking care of children's information and digital image.
Para acompañar a un menor en su vida dig: To accompany a child in their digital life you don't need to be a technology expert, but you do need to know, at least in general terms, where they spend their time: social networks such as Instagram, TikTok or Snapchat, messaging platforms such as WhatsApp or Discord, and video games with a social component such as Roblox, Fortnite or Minecraft, where they often chat with strangers during the game. Each platform has its own risks: some expose location or online status, others allow direct contact from strangers, and several combine both. There's no need to ban their use, but it's worth exploring them yourself, understanding what privacy settings they offer and talking with the child about what they share and whom they interact with on each one.
Un niño de 8 años y un adolescente de 15: An 8-year-old and a 15-year-old don't face the same risks online, nor do they have the same ability to identify them. Younger children are usually vulnerable to inappropriate content and to sharing information without understanding the consequences, while teenagers are more exposed to cyberbullying, social pressure and contact with strangers seeking to gain their trust. Adapting your support to each stage is key: with young children, direct supervision and technical controls work better, while with teenagers it's more effective to build their own judgment through dialogue, since excessive control at that age usually creates rejection and leads them to hide their online activity instead of sharing it.
El ciberacoso es el hostigamiento repeti: Cyberbullying is the repeated harassment of a child through digital means: offensive messages, deliberate exclusion from groups, spreading rumors or posting humiliating images without consent. Unlike in-person bullying, it doesn't stop when they get home, which can intensify its emotional impact. Some warning signs include sudden mood changes after using the phone, avoiding certain apps or devices they used to use normally, sudden social isolation or a noticeable drop in school performance. Detecting it in time depends more on being alert to these behavior changes than on monitoring every message they receive, and it requires opening a space for conversation without judging or minimizing what the child is going through.
La exposición a contenido violento, sexu: Exposure to violent, sexual or simply age-inappropriate content can happen even on platforms designed for children, whether through poorly filtered recommendation algorithms, links shared by other users or misleading advertising. Unlike traditional television, on the internet this content can appear without warning and without an adult present to give context in the moment. Parental controls and content filters help reduce exposure, but don't eliminate it completely, so it's equally important to teach the child what to do if they come across something that makes them uncomfortable: leave the app, don't forward it and tell a trusted adult without fear of being scolded for having seen it.
El grooming es el proceso mediante el cu: Grooming is the process by which an adult progressively gains a child's trust online, with the aim of abusing that relationship. It usually progresses in stages: casual initial contact, compliments and virtual gifts, isolating the child from those close to them, and finally increasingly invasive requests, such as asking for photos or in-person meetings. It frequently happens in video games with chat, social networks and messaging apps, where the adult can pretend to be someone the same age. The best defense isn't banning contact with other people online, but teaching the child that no legitimate trusted adult will ask them to keep secrets, send private photos or meet alone, and that they can tell someone without fear of getting into trouble.
Riesgos específicos como grooming y cibe: Specific risks such as grooming and cyberbullying
Explica qué es el grooming y cómo identi: Explains what grooming is and how to identify risk signs in time.
Presenta las manifestaciones del ciberac: Presents the forms cyberbullying takes and how to recognize them.
Aborda los riesgos de exposición a conte: Covers the risks of exposure to content unsuitable for the child's age.
Las herramientas de control parental, in: Parental control tools, built into the operating system or available as standalone apps, make it possible to limit usage time, block content categories and review which apps the child installs, without needing to read every message they send. Setting them up together with the child's own device, also adjusting the privacy of each social network or game they use (who can see them, contact them or see their location), reduces much of the risk of unwanted exposure. It's important to present them as a support tool and not as covert surveillance: explaining to the child what was set up and why generates far more cooperation than installing them secretly, and keeps them from feeling their trust was betrayed when they eventually find out.
Herramientas de control parental y bueno: Parental control tools and good habits
Enseña a configurar herramientas de cont: Teaches how to set up parental control tools on devices and platforms.
Presenta recomendaciones para establecer: Presents recommendations for setting appropriate screen time limits.
Explica cómo usar las herramientas de re: Explains how to use the reporting and blocking tools available on platforms.
Definir límites de tiempo de pantalla no: Setting screen time limits doesn't aim to eliminate device use, but to keep it from displacing sleep, physical activity and in-person relationships. There's no magic number of hours valid for every age; what matters is observing whether use interferes with other areas of the child's life, such as school performance or general mood. It works better to set limits through conversation rather than imposing them, with clear agreements on schedules (for example, no screens before bed or during meals) and consequences known in advance if they aren't respected. Adults themselves must model these habits: it's hard to ask a teenager to put down their phone at the table if the rest of the family doesn't do the same.
Cómo reportar y bloquear en apps: How to report and block in apps
Prácticamente todas las plataformas popu: Practically every platform popular among children (social networks, games and messaging apps) includes reporting and blocking features, but they're often hidden in unintuitive menus that adults themselves have rarely explored. Knowing in advance how to report inappropriate content, block a user who's harassing and report a fake account makes it possible to act immediately instead of wasting valuable time looking for the option in the middle of an uncomfortable situation for the child. It's worth spending a few minutes reviewing these features in the apps the child uses before a problem occurs, and teaching them directly how to use them, so they don't always depend on an adult to act in the moment.
Cómo conversar sobre seguridad digital: How to talk about digital safety
Hablar de seguridad digital funciona mej: Talking about digital safety works better as an ongoing conversation than as a single, solemn talk. Taking advantage of everyday moments, such as a news story about an online scam or something that happened to a classmate, usually opens the door more naturally than sitting down to "give the internet talk". It's key to use a tone of genuine curiosity rather than interrogation: asking which apps they use, what they like about them and whom they interact with, instead of only warning about dangers. When the child feels they can talk about their digital life without being judged or automatically punished, they're much more likely to turn to an adult in an uncomfortable situation, instead of hiding it for fear of losing access to their devices.
Vigilar cada mensaje, foto o búsqueda de: Monitoring every message, photo or search a child makes may seem like the safest way to protect them, but it usually has the opposite effect: it pushes them to use hidden accounts, friends' devices or apps adults don't know about, precisely to avoid that control. Supervision is necessary, especially with young children, but it should gradually decrease and turn into support as the child grows and shows their own judgment. Building trust means involving them in decisions about their digital life, explaining the reason for each limit instead of imposing it without context, and recognizing when they act well, not just correcting them when they make mistakes. A teenager who trusts they'll be listened to, and not just punished, comes forward sooner when there's a real problem.
Cómo acompañar a los menores en su vida: How to accompany children in their digital life
Ofrece pautas para iniciar conversacione: Offers guidelines for starting open conversations about digital safety.
Explica cómo equilibrar el acompañamient: Explains how to balance support with respect for the child's autonomy.
Presenta cambios de comportamiento que p: Presents behavior changes that may indicate a digital problem.
Existen señales concretas que ameritan u: There are concrete signs that warrant a direct, prompt conversation with a child, without needing to wait for absolute certainty that something is wrong. Among them: suddenly hiding the screen when an adult approaches, receiving gifts or money of unknown origin, mood changes associated with using a specific device or app, social withdrawal, or mentioning a "new friend" online they avoid giving details about. No single sign is definitive proof of a problem, but a combination of several, or a behavior change sustained over time, justifies approaching them calmly, without accusations, and openly asking what's going on before the situation escalates into something harder to handle.
Acompañar emocionalmente tras un inciden: Providing emotional support after an incident
Cuando un menor atraviesa un incidente d: When a child goes through a digital incident, whether cyberbullying, exposure to inappropriate content or contact with an ill-intentioned adult, the responsible adult's initial reaction makes the difference between the child feeling protected or guilty. It's essential to avoid reproach ("why did you do that?") and prioritize emotional support: validating what they feel, making it clear they're not in trouble for telling you, and conveying calm even if you're worried inside. A disproportionate reaction, such as immediately taking away the device as punishment, usually teaches the child that reporting a problem has negative consequences, which makes them less likely to ask for help next time. If the emotional impact persists, seeking professional psychological support is a valid and recommended step.
Dónde denunciar un incidente digital: Where to report a digital incident
Además de reportar dentro de la propia p: Besides reporting within the platform where the incident happened, there are specialized channels for serious cases such as grooming, child sexual exploitation or severe cyberbullying: national hotlines dedicated to protecting children online, police units specialized in computer crimes, and non-governmental organizations that offer guidance and legal support to families. Knowing these resources before you need them saves critical time in a crisis, when acting quickly may be important to preserve evidence or stop active contact with the child. Saving screenshots, conversations and the profiles involved, without deleting anything before reporting, greatly facilitates the subsequent investigation by the competent authorities.

Qué hacer ante ciberacoso o grooming: What to do in cases of cyberbullying or grooming
Ante una sospecha o confirmación de cibe: When cyberbullying or grooming is suspected or confirmed, the first step is to listen to the child without interrupting or judging, and assure them they did the right thing by telling you. Next, it's advisable to document the available evidence (screenshots, usernames, dates) before blocking the aggressor, since blocking first can make that information inaccessible. The next step is to report within the platform and, if the situation involves an adult contacting a child or serious threats, report it to the competent authorities without delay. Throughout the process, keeping the child informed in an age-appropriate way about what's happening, without excluding them from decisions that directly affect them, helps them not feel they've lost control of the situation.

No todo contacto en línea es un amigo re: Not every online contact is a real friend
Un amigo real es alguien que conoces en: A real friend is someone you know in person, someone you've played with, shared a hug or a laugh with, and whom your family also knows; an online contact, on the other hand, is someone you've only seen through a screen, and even though they may sometimes seem very nice, the truth is you don't know for sure who's really on the other side of that photo or name. This doesn't mean all online contacts are bad, but it does mean you have to be more careful with them, because a person can pretend to be a kid your age when they're actually an adult with bad intentions. That's why it's so important not to accept just anyone who writes to you in a game or on a social network as a "friend", and to tell a trusted adult if someone you don't know in person keeps insisting on talking to you or asks you for photos and personal details.
Primeros pasos para entender internet y: First steps to understanding the internet and my information
Introduce de forma sencilla qué es inter: Introduces in a simple way what the internet is and how it's used in daily life.
Enseña a los menores a valorar y cuidar: Teaches children to value and take care of their personal information.
Ayuda a distinguir entre relaciones de c: Helps distinguish between trusted relationships and unknown contacts online.
Tu información personal vale mucho, cuíd: Your personal information is worth a lot, take care of it
Tu nombre completo, tu dirección, el col: Your full name, your address, the school you go to, your phone number and even photos you appear in: all of that is personal information, and it's like a treasure that only you and your family should decide whom to show. When you're on the internet, playing or chatting, sometimes someone may ask you for that information while pretending to be a friendly person, but just as you wouldn't give the key to your house to a stranger on the street, you shouldn't give your personal information to someone you only know through a screen. For example, if a game asks for your address to "send you a prize", that's a warning sign, because serious game companies almost never need that information for you to keep playing. Taking care of your treasure means thinking twice before sharing it and, if you're not sure, always asking a trusted adult before typing any of your details.
Qué es internet y cómo forma parte de tu: What the internet is and how it's part of your day
Internet es como una gran red que conect: The internet is like a big network that connects computers, tablets and phones all over the world, letting you watch videos, play with friends who live far away, do school homework or video call your family, all from a screen. Even if you don't notice, you use the internet many times a day, from when you look up information for homework to when you watch your favorite show or play an online video game with other players. The internet itself isn't good or bad; it's a tool, a bit like a bicycle, that can take you to wonderful places if you use it carefully, but that also requires learning certain rules so you don't get hurt, like wearing a helmet when you ride a bike. Knowing how the internet works and what you use it for every day is the first step to learning how to move around it safely while enjoying all the good things it has to offer.
Cómo crear contraseñas fuertes y mantene: How to create strong passwords and keep them secret
Una contraseña es como la llave secreta: A password is like the secret key to your account, and just as you wouldn't lend the key to your house to just anyone, you shouldn't share your password with anyone, not even your best friend, because once another person knows it, it's not really secret anymore. For a password to be strong and hard to guess, it's best to mix uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers and a symbol, and not use something obvious like your name or your birthday, which anyone could find out just by looking at your profile. A fun trick is to think of a phrase you like, such as your pet's name together with your favorite food and a special number, to create something easy for you to remember but almost impossible for someone else to guess, and it's always a good idea to tell a trusted adult where you keep your passwords in case you ever forget them.
Cómo cuidar mis contraseñas y mi privaci: How to take care of my passwords and my privacy
Enseña de forma lúdica a crear contraseñ: Teaches in a playful way how to create strong passwords and keep them private.
Presenta ejemplos claros de información: Presents clear examples of information that should never be shared publicly.
Explica cómo ajustar la privacidad en re: Explains how to adjust privacy settings on social networks and video games.
Cómo proteger tu privacidad en redes y v: How to protect your privacy on social networks and video games
La privacidad significa decidir quién pu: Privacy means deciding who can see your information, your photos and what you post, and on social networks or video games there are special settings, called privacy settings, that let you choose for only your real friends or your family to see your profile, instead of leaving it open for any stranger in the world to look at. Many platforms come set up more openly by default than they should be, so it's a good idea for an adult to help you review those settings together as soon as you create a new account, instead of leaving them as they were at the start without checking them. For example, in an online game you can choose not to show your location to other players, or on a social network you can hide your friends list so nobody you don't know can see whom you talk to, small decisions that help keep your digital life much safer and just for the people you trust.
Cosas que nunca debes compartir en inter: Things you should never share on the internet
Hay ciertas cosas que nunca deberías com: There are certain things you should never share on the internet, no matter who asks or how much they insist, such as your exact address, the name of your school, your phone number, your passwords or photos of yourself without clothes or in private situations. Even if sharing something seems like just one more message, once something leaves your computer or phone and goes onto the internet, you can no longer control who sees it, saves it or shares it later, even if the other person promised only they would see it. An example is when someone in a game asks "what school do you go to" supposedly to see if you're at the same one, and although it sounds innocent, that information together with other clues can help a stranger find you in real life. The simplest rule is that, if you're not sure whether something is safe to share, the right answer is almost always to ask a trusted adult first before sending it.
Cómo reconocer señales de peligro en lín: How to recognize signs of danger online
Ayuda a identificar qué significa intera: Helps identify what it means to interact with a stranger online.
Presenta señales de alerta ante situacio: Presents warning signs in uncomfortable or suspicious situations.
Explica de forma sencilla qué es el cibe: Explains in a simple way what cyberbullying is and how to recognize it.
Cómo reconocer el ciberacoso y qué hacer: How to recognize cyberbullying and what to do
El ciberacoso ocurre cuando alguien usa: Cyberbullying happens when someone uses the internet, a chat or a social network to bother, make fun of, threaten or make another person feel bad over and over again, such as sending hurtful messages, sharing an embarrassing photo without permission or deliberately leaving someone out of a group chat to make them feel bad. Unlike a normal argument between friends that gets fixed quickly, cyberbullying happens again and again and is meant to hurt, and it can be even harder to escape because the messages can reach you at any moment, even when you're in your own home. Recognizing it is the first step to stopping it, so if you see that someone keeps bothering you online, or that it's happening to a classmate, what matters is not responding with more aggression, saving the messages as evidence if you can, and telling a trusted adult right away so they can help you sort it out.
Cómo reconocer a un desconocido en inter: How to recognize a stranger on the internet
Un extraño en internet es cualquier pers: A stranger on the internet is anyone you don't know in real life, even if they seem very nice in the chat, share funny photos or say they're your age, because on the internet anyone can write whatever they want about who they are, and sometimes the person behind the screen isn't who they say they are. This doesn't mean all strangers are dangerous, but it does mean you need to be as careful with them as you would be with a stranger who approaches you in the park, without giving personal information or agreeing to meet in person without an adult knowing. One sign to recognize them is when someone you just met in a game or on a social network starts asking lots of questions about where you live, what school you go to or asks you for photos, and if that happens, the best thing is to stop answering and tell a trusted adult right away.
Cómo notar señales de alerta en internet: How to notice warning signs on the internet
Así como en la vida real notamos cuando: Just as in real life we notice when something feels strange or uncomfortable, on the internet there are also signs that warn us something isn't right, such as when someone insists too much that you keep a secret, asks you not to tell your parents about a conversation, or makes you feel pressured to do something you don't want to do. Another important sign is when someone offers you gifts, virtual money or special prizes in exchange for photos, personal information or doing something that makes you uncomfortable, because people with good intentions don't need to ask for those kinds of things in return. Learning to notice these signs is like developing a little internal alarm detector, and trusting that "this doesn't feel right" feeling is always valid, so if you ever feel it, the best thing is to stop answering and tell a trusted adult immediately, without feeling afraid or embarrassed to do so.
Saber a quién acudir si algo te incomoda: Knowing whom to turn to if something online makes you uncomfortable
Si alguna vez algo que ves o que te dice: If anything you see or are told on the internet ever makes you feel weird, sad, scared or just uncomfortable, the most important thing to know is that you're never alone and there's always a trusted adult you can tell what happened, whether it's your mom, your dad, a teacher, an uncle or any grown-up you feel safe with. Telling someone what makes you uncomfortable isn't "tattling" or getting yourself into trouble; on the contrary, it's the bravest way to take care of yourself, and it can also help keep it from happening to other children. Sometimes it's a little embarrassing to tell certain things, but trusted adults are there precisely to help you without getting angry with you, so if something in a game, a chat or a photo made you feel bad, tell someone in your family or at your school right away, even if you're not completely sure whether it was serious or not.
Cómo usar las herramientas de bloquear y: How to use the block and report tools
Casi todas las aplicaciones, juegos y re: Almost all apps, games and social networks have two very useful tools to keep you safe, blocking and reporting, and learning to use them is like having a magic button to protect yourself when someone bothers you or makes you feel uncomfortable online. Blocking a person means they can no longer write to you or see what you post, and reporting means letting the platform know that someone is doing something that breaks the rules, so they can review it and take action. You don't have to feel afraid or guilty about using these tools; on the contrary, they're part of taking care of yourself, just like walking away from someone who treats you badly in the schoolyard. A good habit is that, every time you block or report someone, you also tell a trusted adult, so they know what happened and can help you if the situation needs more than just blocking that person.

Detente y piensa antes de hacer clic en: Stop and think before clicking on something
Antes de hacer clic en un enlace, acepta: Before clicking a link, accepting a friend request or sharing a photo, it's worth stopping for a moment and thinking, because once you click or send something, you can't undo it so easily, just like when you say something you later wish you hadn't said. A good trick is to ask yourself simple questions before acting, such as whether you really know the person who sent you that link, whether the message sounds too good to be true, or whether you'd feel comfortable showing that photo or message to your family. For example, if you get a message saying you won an amazing prize just by clicking a link, that's almost always a trap to trick you, because real prizes don't work that way. Taking those few extra seconds to think before acting is one of the best habits you can build to browse the internet safely and without nasty surprises.

Cómo disfrutar juegos y apps sin correr: How to enjoy games and apps without taking risks
Jugar videojuegos, ver videos o usar apl: Playing video games, watching videos or using educational apps can be lots of fun and can even help you learn new things, but to keep it safe it's worth following a few simple habits, such as only using apps an adult has checked or downloaded, and not clicking on windows that suddenly pop up promising prizes or free levels. Those pop-up windows are often traps to get you to download something harmful onto the device or to share information without realizing it, so if something looks strange or too good to be true, the best thing is to close that window and ask an adult before touching any button. Playing safely also means taking care of how much time you spend in front of the screen and letting people at home know which games or apps you're using, so the whole family can enjoy technology together without nasty surprises.
Trata a los demás bien también en intern: Treat others well on the internet too
Las mismas reglas de buena convivencia q: The same rules for getting along that you use at school or with your friends, like not making fun of someone, saying please or apologizing when you make a mistake, also apply when you're on the internet, chatting, playing online or commenting on social networks. Sometimes it seems that, because we don't see the other person's face, words hurt less, but in reality behind every message there's a real person who can feel sad or hurt just like you, so before writing something it's good to ask yourself whether you'd say it to that person face to face. Being kind online also means not forwarding gossip or jokes about other classmates, and if you see someone being treated badly in a chat or game, you can be brave and say that's not okay, or simply tell an adult so they can help sort it out.
Pasar tiempo frente a una pantalla, juga: Spending time in front of a screen, playing, watching videos or talking with friends, can be fun and even useful for learning, but as with any good thing, it's important to find a balance so there's also time to play outside, read, sleep well and be with your family without a screen in between. When we spend too many hours in a row online, we can feel more tired, grumpy or have trouble sleeping, and often we don't even notice how much time has gone by until someone tells us. A good habit is to set limits together with your family, such as using a timer to know when to take a break, or agreeing on times of the day without screens, like during meals, to enjoy the other fun things that also exist outside the internet more, without meaning you have to stop enjoying your favorite games and videos.

Reglas que definen cómo trabajar seguro: Rules that define how to work securely remotely
Cada organización que permite trabajo re: Every organization that allows remote work usually has a set of rules defining which devices you can use, which networks are acceptable, how to access internal systems and what to do in the event of an incident, although many people never read them carefully. These policies don't exist to complicate day-to-day work, but because outside the office the company loses much of the technical control it has over its own network, and needs clear rules to keep information protected no matter where you connect from. Knowing them saves you from awkward situations, such as using an unauthorized tool to share an urgent file and unintentionally causing a security breach. An important nuance is that these policies are usually updated as threats change, so reviewing them from time to time, and not just when you start the job, helps you stay aligned with what the organization expects of you as a remote employee.
Qué le corresponde cuidar a cada persona: What each person is responsible for protecting remotely
Cuando trabajas fuera de la oficina, bue: When you work outside the office, much of the security the IT team used to take care of now depends directly on you, and understanding what you're responsible for is key to not leaving gaps uncovered. This includes concrete things, such as keeping your device up to date, using only authorized networks and tools, physically protecting work devices when you leave home and reporting any suspicious sign as soon as you detect it, instead of waiting to confirm it really was a problem. It's not about becoming a security expert, but about accepting that certain everyday decisions, such as where you connect or whom you share a file with, now carry a weight that used to fall on the office infrastructure. Organizations usually document these responsibilities clearly precisely because they know the strongest link in the remote security chain is an informed, attentive employee, not just the technology they use.
Amenazas propias de trabajar fuera de la: Threats specific to working outside the office
Trabajar desde casa o desde cualquier lu: Working from home or anywhere outside the office suddenly removes several layers of protection we normally don't even notice, such as the monitored corporate network, physical control over who enters the building or technical support just a few steps away. Instead, we depend on a home network that may never have been configured with security in mind, on personal devices mixed with work, and on our own attention to detect fraud attempts without the immediate backing of an IT team. Added to this, teleworking encourages distraction and haste, ideal conditions for falling for a well-disguised phishing email or sharing a file through the wrong channel. Understanding these risks isn't meant to create fear, but to help you consciously rebuild, in your own space, some of the protections the office offered automatically, such as a secure network, verification habits and knowing whom to notify if something goes wrong.
Cómo borrar tu información antes de entr: How to erase your information before handing over your phone
Cuando cambias de teléfono, ya sea para: When you change phones, whether to sell, give away or dispose of the old one, it's easy to focus on transferring data to the new device and forget that the old one still stores photos, saved passwords and active sessions for your accounts. A poorly done factory reset, or simply deleting the visible files, doesn't always erase information irrecoverably, especially if the device wasn't encrypted beforehand. The right process starts with backing up whatever you want to keep, signing out of all accounts and unlinking the device from services such as Find My iPhone or your Google account, so the new owner isn't locked out and you're no longer associated with the device. After that, a factory reset on an already encrypted phone leaves the data practically unrecoverable, which is exactly why enabling encryption from day one makes this moment much easier when it finally comes.
Ajustar qué información comparte tu móvi: Adjusting what information your phone shares
Los teléfonos modernos recopilan una can: Modern phones collect an enormous amount of information about us, from our exact location to our contacts, photos and usage habits, and much of that data is shared with apps without us noticing. Reviewing privacy settings isn't a complicated technical exercise, but a periodic review of which apps have access to your location, camera, microphone or files, and whether that access makes sense for what they actually do. Location deserves special attention because many apps request it permanently when they only need it while in use, and leaving it on all the time makes it possible to build a detailed map of your daily routines. Most operating systems already let you choose between permanent access, only while the app is in use, or never, and choosing the most restrictive option by default significantly reduces the information you end up exposing without realizing it.

Cómo equilibrar trabajo y vida personal: How to balance work and personal life on the same phone
Cada vez más organizaciones permiten usa: More and more organizations allow employees to use their personal phone for work, a model known as BYOD, which is convenient but mixes two worlds that are best kept separate. When the same device stores both your family photos and corporate email or company apps, a security incident on one side can end up affecting the other, and the organization needs a certain level of control over data that belongs to it even if it's on your personal device. Many companies solve this with device management apps that create a separate, encrypted space just for work, without touching your photos or personal apps, or with independent work profiles within the same phone. It's worth understanding what access your employer has to the device under this policy, for example whether it can remotely wipe only corporate data or the whole phone, so you can use your phone with confidence and without surprises.
Ajustes básicos para proteger tu red de: Basic settings to protect your home network
El router de tu casa es la puerta de ent: Your home router is the entry point for every device you use for work, and yet many people never change its factory settings, leaving active the default password printed on the device, which anyone can look up online if they know the model. Changing that password to a strong one, both for accessing the router and for connecting to the Wi-Fi, is one of the most important and least applied settings in homes. It's also worth keeping the router's firmware up to date, something many manufacturers do automatically nowadays but that's worth confirming, and disabling features you don't use, such as remote access to the router's administration from the internet. A practical nuance is creating a separate network for guests or smart home devices, so a connected appliance with weak security doesn't share the same network as your work computer.

Por qué no mezclar equipos personales y: Why not to mix personal and work devices
Usar la misma computadora para revisar c: Using the same computer to check work email, watch shows and let the kids do their homework seems practical, but it mixes the lowest level of security in the home with the company's most sensitive information. A personal device usually has fewer controls, more apps installed by different family members and greater exposure to risky downloads, which increases the likelihood of malware ending up close to corporate files. When the organization provides a dedicated work device, using it exclusively for that purpose, without installing personal programs or sharing it with other people in the home, keeps that environment more controlled and predictable. If that option doesn't exist and you must use your own computer, at least creating a separate user account just for work, with its own passwords and no shared access, considerably reduces the risk of a personal slip ending up affecting company information.
Para qué sirve conectarte por VPN al tra: What connecting through a VPN is for when working
La VPN corporativa crea un túnel cifrado: The corporate VPN creates an encrypted tunnel between your device and the company's internal systems, so even if you're connected from home or a café, the traffic travels protected as if you were physically inside the office network. This is especially important for accessing internal systems that should never be directly exposed on the internet, such as file servers or administrative applications, since the VPN acts as an additional barrier against anyone trying to intercept that connection. A common mistake is connecting to the VPN just fifteen minutes before a specific task and disconnecting the rest of the time, when the recommendation is usually to keep it active throughout the remote workday, following the organization's policy. It's also worth remembering that the VPN protects the connection but doesn't replace other precautions such as up-to-date antivirus or being wary of suspicious emails, so it's still one more piece in a set of good practices, not a single solution.
Por qué mantener al día los equipos de t: Why keep work devices up to date
Cuando trabajas fuera de la oficina, tu: When you work outside the office, your device is no longer constantly connected to the corporate network that used to apply updates and security patches almost invisibly for you. That means part of that responsibility now falls on your own habits, such as not indefinitely postponing update notices for the operating system or work apps, even when they appear at an inconvenient moment during a busy workday. Every pending update is a known security flaw that remains open, and attackers often take advantage of precisely that window of time in which remote devices take longer to receive patches than those in the office. Many organizations use remote management software that pushes updates automatically, but when that doesn't happen, regularly checking for and applying updates yourself is one of the simplest and most effective ways to protect your work device.
Cómo iniciar sesión de forma segura a di: How to log in securely from a distance
Cuando trabajas fuera de la oficina, la: When you work outside the office, the password is no longer the only barrier between an attacker and the company's systems, because you no longer have the protection of the corporate network around you. That's why multi-factor authentication, that additional code that arrives on your phone or that an app generates, becomes so important, since even if someone manages to steal your password, they won't be able to get in without that second element. A common slip is approving login notifications out of habit, without checking whether it was really you who tried to log in, which completely cancels out the second factor's protection. It's also worth using different passwords for each system and avoiding storing them in notes or browsers without additional protection, relying instead on a trustworthy password manager. Managing your remote access well means treating each login with the same attention you would if someone knocked on the office door asking to come in.
Cómo cuidar el equipo que usas para trab: How to take care of the device you use for work
Ya sea que la empresa te dé un equipo de: Whether the company gives you a dedicated device or you work from your own device under a BYOD policy, there are basic habits that protect both corporate information and your personal peace of mind. Keeping the device locked when you're not using it, even at home, avoiding installing software without checking where it comes from and not plugging in unknown USB drives are simple measures that reduce much of the everyday risk. On corporate devices, respecting the restrictions the IT department imposes, even if they're sometimes inconvenient, has an underlying reason: those settings exist because someone already analyzed the specific risks of your role. In the case of BYOD, understanding what the company can see or control on your own device, usually limited to a separate work app or profile, helps you use it with confidence without feeling you're losing personal privacy. In both cases, reporting any sign of malfunction immediately keeps a small problem from escalating without anyone noticing in time.

Cómo cuidar papeles y archivos de trabaj: How to take care of work papers and files at home
Trabajar desde casa cambia por completo: Working from home completely changes the environment in which company documents circulate, and it's easy to let your guard down because the space feels private, although in reality family members, visitors or even household staff who shouldn't have access to confidential information live there or pass through. A printed document with customer data left on the desk, or an unprotected home printer connected to the same network other household devices use, can expose information that at the office would be protected by physical controls. The practical recommendation is to minimize printing sensitive documents whenever possible and, when it's necessary, keep them under lock and key or destroy them properly instead of throwing them in the regular trash. It's also worth reviewing the printer's settings, since some keep digital copies of what's printed or are exposed if they have no password, a detail rarely checked in a home environment.
Cuidar lo que se ve y escucha en llamada: Taking care of what's seen and heard on work calls
Cuando trabajas desde casa, tu entorno p: When you work from home, your personal surroundings unintentionally become the visible background of your video calls and the sound environment of your work phone conversations, which can expose information without you realizing it. A whiteboard with internal notes, an open document on the desk or even a family photo with identifiable details in the background can attract the wrong attention during a meeting with external clients. Likewise, talking about confidential topics out loud near open windows or in shared spaces of the home risks someone overhearing information that shouldn't leave that context. Using virtual backgrounds, choosing a fixed spot for work calls and letting the people you live with know when you're in an important meeting are simple adjustments that make a real difference. Taking care of this kind of privacy isn't exaggerating; it's recognizing that the home office is still, for practical purposes, a workspace.
Cómo proteger tus reuniones virtuales de: How to protect your virtual meetings from intruders
Las videollamadas se volvieron parte cen: Video calls became a central part of remote work, and with them came risks that didn't exist before, such as outsiders slipping into a meeting through a carelessly shared link or a room without a password. Setting up a waiting room, requiring an access password and avoiding posting the link in open channels are simple measures that drastically reduce the chance of someone uninvited hearing the company's confidential information. It's also worth checking what you're sharing on screen before starting, because it's easy to forget a tab with emails or sensitive documents open in the background while sharing your entire desktop. Another important nuance is checking who's still connected before discussing sensitive topics, since sometimes a participant forgets to leave or stays connected from an unidentified device. Recording meetings also involves responsibility, so it's best to always let participants know and store those recordings only in the spaces authorized by the organization.
Cómo enviar documentos de trabajo sin ri: How to send work documents without risks
Compartir un archivo de trabajo parece u: Sharing a work file seems like a simple gesture, but the channel you choose largely determines who else might see that content. Sending a document with customer data through a personal chat or a free email account, instead of the approved corporate platform, takes that information out of the environment the company controls and places it in a space without the same security or backup guarantees. Before sharing, it's worth asking yourself whether the person receiving the file really needs it, and whether the level of access you give them, such as read-only instead of full editing, matches what their work requires. A useful habit is setting an expiration date on shared links when the tool allows it, so access doesn't stay open indefinitely after the original need has passed, something very few people check once the file has served its purpose.

Cómo y cuándo avisar si algo sale mal en: How and when to speak up if something goes wrong remotely
Cuando notas algo raro trabajando desde: When you notice something strange while working from home, such as a suspicious email you've already opened, a file you don't recognize or unusual access to your account, the temptation is to solve it yourself or wait until you're back at the office to mention it, but that delay is exactly what most benefits an attacker. Outside the office environment the IT team isn't just around the corner, so it's best to know in advance what the reporting channel is, whether an email, a chat or a contact number, and not waste time looking for it right when the incident has already happened. Reporting quickly, even if you're not sure it's serious, is always better than staying quiet for fear of overreacting or being reprimanded, because many incidents that are controlled in time only become serious because of a delay in reporting them. Keeping that emergency contact handy, just as you would a technical support number, is simple preparation that makes all the difference when it's really needed.
Cómo trabajar en equipo sin exponer info: How to work as a team without exposing information
Las herramientas de colaboración en la n: Cloud collaboration tools, such as shared documents, task boards or team chats, make remote work enormously easier, but they also multiply the places where company information can be exposed if they aren't configured carefully. A frequent mistake is leaving a document with edit permissions open to anyone with the link, instead of restricting it to the specific people who really need it, which turns an internal file into something practically public. It's also worth periodically reviewing which third-party integrations have access to these platforms, since apps connected long ago and forgotten may still have permissions over sensitive information without anyone remembering. Using only the tools approved by the organization, instead of personal solutions for convenience, and checking the access level before sharing any file are simple habits that prevent leaks that are later hard to trace and fix.
Por qué mantener el móvil siempre actual: Why keep your phone always up to date
Cada actualización del sistema operativo: Every operating system update, besides bringing new features, fixes security flaws that attackers already know about and are actively exploiting. When you put off an update for weeks, you don't just miss out on improvements; you leave open a door the manufacturer has already closed for other users. This is especially critical on phones because they usually go everywhere with us, connected to different networks and with access to email, banking and work apps. Turning on automatic updates, for both the system and apps, is the simplest way to stay protected without having to think about it constantly. An important nuance is that very old devices stop receiving security patches at some point, even if they still work fine, so a phone that no longer receives updates represents a silent risk worth keeping in mind when deciding whether to replace it.
Cómo varían los riesgos entre iOS y Andr: How risks vary between iOS and Android
iOS y Android abordan la seguridad de fo: iOS and Android approach security differently, and understanding those differences helps you make better decisions no matter which one you use. iOS is a more closed system, where Apple strictly controls which apps get into the store and limits each app's access to the rest of the system, which reduces the room for accidentally installing malicious software. Android, being more open and used by multiple manufacturers, offers greater flexibility and customization, but that also means more variety of versions, updates that don't always arrive on time from every brand, and the possibility of installing apps outside the official store, something much more restricted on iOS. Neither is inherently insecure if used carefully, but each calls for a different approach, such as prioritizing the manufacturer's updates on Android or avoiding forcing the installation of apps from outside the store on either one.
